sections.html:
Selling a house in Bremerton starts with the Navy. The city of 45,482 residents (July 1, 2025) is the largest on the Kitsap Peninsula and is home to Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and the Bremerton Annex of Naval Base Kitsap. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $439,400. Fewer than half of households own, which means plenty of houses are rentals. Owners here choose between an agent, a sale by owner, and a cash buyer.

Housing measureBremerton figure
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 202448.1%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024$439,400
Median gross rent, 2020 to 2024$1,641
Median household income, 2020 to 2024$74,940
Population, 2020 Census43,505

Commute routes decide which blocks sell fastest. The Port Washington Narrows cuts the city in two, and two bridges join the halves: the Warren Avenue Bridge on State Route 303, opened in 1958, and the Manette Bridge, rebuilt in 2011. State Route 3 runs as a freeway through the west side, and a tunnel carries ferry traffic from the terminal to State Route 304.

Washington State Ferries takes about an hour from Bremerton to Seattle, and Kitsap Transit's passenger-only fast ferry covers the crossing in 28 minutes. Shipyard workers and Seattle commuters will ask how far the house is from the terminal or the gates.

  • Downtown and the waterfront have new apartments, restored older buildings and the Admiral Theatre.
  • Manette sits on its own peninsula and reaches downtown over the Manette Bridge.
  • Charleston centers on Callow Avenue.
  • Union Hill is mostly residential, between downtown and Charleston.
  • Evergreen has water views and a park with a beach and boat ramp.
  • Haddon surrounds Bremerton High School and the Olympic College campus.

Three school districts reach into the city: Bremerton, Central Kitsap and South Kitsap. Check which one applies to your address before naming a school in the listing.

Rainfall averages 56.93 inches a year, while snow averages about 3 inches. With that much water, roofs, gutters, siding, crawl spaces and drainage deserve attention before a showing or an inspection, especially on an older house.

Anyone who rents or leases real property inside Bremerton limits needs a City of Bremerton Landlord Business License under BMC 3.48.025. It is a city license, separate from any Washington state business license, and it costs $75 a year. Each license covers a calendar year and must be renewed by January 31.

  • Renting rooms inside your own home counts as rental activity.
  • A relative living in your house counts as a rental even if no rent is paid, unless you live there more than half the year.
  • Landlords join the Landlord Notification Program (BMC 5.06) by giving the Police Department a list of rentals and a contact method.
  • Landlords certify that units meet RCW 59.18.060, and the city does not run physical inspections.
  • Stays under 30 days, such as vacation rentals, fall under state business licensing instead.

An unlicensed property can limit the owner's ability to pursue an eviction. If you inherited a Bremerton rental, bring the license in line before you list it, and call the Tax and License Division at 360-473-5311 with questions.

Excise tax on the sale is the seller's cost, collected by the Kitsap County Treasurer. Kitsap lists the local portion at 0.50 percent, and the state portion is graduated. Because a home at Bremerton's median value sits under the $525,000 first band, the state portion there is the lowest rate, 1.1 percent. A $5 state technology fee is added. Ask the treasurer to confirm the total for your parcel.

  • Payment is due within 30 days of the date on the conveying document, and the deed cannot be recorded until it is paid.
  • Seller and buyer, or an agent for each, sign the Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit.
  • The treasurer takes cash or check payable to the Kitsap County Treasurer, and cards carry fees.
  • Late payment adds interest and penalties under RCW 82.45.100, which reach 20 percent of the tax after three months.

From January 1, 2027 the state's three break points rise to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000.

Kitsap splits the bill into halves due April 30 and October 31, honoring the postmark. Anything at $50 or less is a single April payment. For residential property with four or fewer units, delinquent tax carries interest of 0.75 percent a month, which works out to the nine percent a year in RCW 84.56.020. Not receiving a statement does not erase interest.

If you refinanced recently, check the account. Kitsap warns that tax money collected at a refinance is sometimes not forwarded to the treasurer until April or October, so confirm it shows as paid before you list. The Assessor's Office at (360) 337-5777 handles the senior and disabled exemption and deferral, the limited-income deferral, the residential improvement exemption and the destroyed property exemption. State law also bars interest and penalties on the home of an active duty service member stationed outside the United States during a period of armed conflict.

Orders to a new duty station, an inherited rental or a house that needs work all push owners toward a faster sale. The routes are familiar.

  • List with an agent and time showings around the crowds that fill downtown for events such as the Armed Forces Day parade in May and the Blackberry Festival over Labor Day.
  • Sell the house yourself, handling the disclosure statement and the excise tax affidavit on your own.
  • Ask a cash buyer for an offer on the house as it stands, so you skip repairs and open houses.

On every route the buyer is owed a seller disclosure statement, five business days after signing, unless waived or exempt. Under RCW 64.06.020 the buyer can rescind for three business days after getting it.

sections.h2: Confirming city limits and closing steps
sections.html: Enter the address in the Kitsap County Parcel Search, the tool the city points owners to. City limits decide whether the landlord license and other city rules apply. After that, the path runs as follows: accept an offer, open escrow, let title work surface any unpaid tax, sign the affidavit and deed, and pay excise tax to the treasurer before recording. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, so a transfer for a house that needs work can close on a short calendar once the paperwork is ready.

faqs.q: How much does a Bremerton seller pay in excise tax?
faqs.a: That depends on price. The state share begins at 1.1 percent of the first $525,000, Kitsap adds a local 0.50 percent, and there is a $5 state technology fee.

faqs.q: Does Bremerton require a license to rent out a house?
faqs.a: Yes. Anyone renting real property inside city limits needs a Bremerton Landlord Business License, which costs $75 a year and renews by January 31. The city does not inspect the unit and relies on the landlord's certification.

faqs.q: When are Kitsap County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due April 30 and half October 31, judged by postmark. A bill of $50 or less is paid in full in April.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bremerton house I inherited with tenants inside?
faqs.a: Yes, but confirm the Landlord Business License is current first, because an unlicensed property can limit the owner's eviction options. Review the lease and ask the Tax and License Division at 360-473-5311 about the license record.

faqs.q: How can I confirm a house is inside Bremerton city limits?
faqs.a: Enter the address in the Kitsap County Parcel Search, the tool the city points owners to. City limits decide whether the landlord license and other city rules apply.
